src/business/model/Member.ts: `@Column()` on property `id` defines database column mapping, which is persistence (infrastructure) mapping.
src/business/model/Member.ts: `canBorrow(openLoans)` is a legitimate domain rule, so this part fits the business layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Member is a domain entity in the business layer. Its business rule, canBorrow (an active member below maxLoans), belongs in the domain. But the class also handles ORM persistence mapping. The TypeORM @Entity() decorator on the class and the @Column() decorator on id define how the entity maps to database tables and columns. That mapping is the job of the persistence (infrastructure) layer. This is a misplaced responsibility, not just an import direction issue: the domain class itself states persistence schema metadata. The mapping should live in the persistence layer, for example in a separate ORM entity or an EntitySchema with a mapper.
